changes.title: Wednesday settled higher, Asia faded on peace talk headlines, and the inventory report drew crude against flat surveys
changes.delta: Wednesday settles: Brent $115.32 (was $113.88 Tuesday), WTI $102.78 (was $99.90); Brent to WTI spread $12.54 (was $13.98). Asia at 0351 GMT Thu: Brent $114.10, WTI $101.45 (Reuters). EIA w/e Oct 23: crude -1.892 Mbbl against surveys at flat (private survey -2.031); gasoline +3.870 against expected draws; distillate -1.462. Diesel crack $90.58, a fifth close below $100. Canadian file is the Oct 27 settle: TMW Dec26 -$31.00 on 2 lots.
changes.body: Brent settled at $115.32, up $1.44, and WTI at $102.78, up $2.88 (settles, Oct 28), and futures held their gains after the inventory report. Overnight, Asia traded Brent at $114.10 and WTI at $101.45 at 0351 GMT (Reuters, Oct 29), down about 1.1 and 1.3 percent, on a US letter to Tehran seeking to revive negotiations and a Qatari draft deal a senior Iranian official dismissed, against reporting that the United States has warned Gulf states to prepare for a possible campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms. The EIA report for the week ending Oct 23 drew crude by 1.892 Mbbl to 410.625 Mbbl, close to the private survey's 2.031 Mbbl draw and far from the analyst surveys at essentially flat. Gasoline built 3.870 Mbbl to 209.180 Mbbl against surveys expecting a draw, distillate drew 1.462 Mbbl to 102.824 Mbbl, refinery utilization slipped to 92.8 percent with PADD 2 at 88.1 percent, and US production rose 723 kb/d to 13.992 Mb/d as storm shut-ins returned. One flow caveat rides with the print: Kpler's lead oil analyst told Reuters the agency appears to have significantly overestimated crude exports, with observed loadings about 1 Mb/d lower than the reported 4.854 Mb/d. The diesel crack printed $90.58 on the validated history refreshed this edition, a fifth straight close below $100 (3-2-1: $48.82). The Canadian settlement file for this edition is the Oct 27 EOD file: December WCS at -$31.00 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 27) on 2 lots, January at -$29.30 on 235 lots, and the December export spread at +$7.57 with both legs traded.
changes.balance: Flat price is trading the escalation calendar in both directions while the inventory data quietly loosen at the edges: crude draws, but gasoline builds into falling demand, production is restored, and the Midwest runs softer. The buffers that remain thin are product stocks and the strategic reserve, not crude supply.
changes.conditional: A Saudi or Aramco statement of damage at Ras Tanura, or loading evidence of a flow interruption, converts two days of claim pricing into a supply event. Continued silence with normal loadings closes the item on this cycle's pattern. A December WCS print on real volume at or beyond -$31.00 confirms the thin settle's level; a sharp narrowing on volume says the 2 lot print was the extreme.
changes.source: Reuters, Oct 28 to 29, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Oct 28, 2026; EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report released Oct 28, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 27, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Oct 29, 2026

changes.title: The heavy barrel from the buyer's side: record refining margins, freight as the pressure, and a corrected earnings calendar
changes.delta: Phillips 66 Q3: earnings $5.616 billion, realized refining margin $38.00/bbl at 98 percent utilization, Central Corridor inputs a record 848 kb/d. Its marketing executive: heavy crude is a race to the bottom, pressured mostly by freight; each $1 of WCS widening is worth $140 million a year to the company. Calendar correction: Cenovus Q3 is Nov 4 (company announcement, Oct 28), not Oct 30; Imperial is confirmed Oct 30.
changes.body: Phillips 66 reported third quarter earnings of $5.616 billion on Wednesday (Oct 28), with refining earnings of $6.031 billion, a worldwide realized refining margin of $38.00/bbl at 98 percent crude capacity utilization, and Central Corridor inputs at a record 848 kb/d. On the call, its executive vice president for marketing and commercial said heavy crude pricing is essentially a race to the bottom for Canadian and Venezuelan volumes, pressured mostly by freight after an initial phase of refinery issues, with more Venezuelan crude on the market and winter diluent blending in Canadian crude starting. Canadian crude is currently favored by the company, the largest US importer of it, and each $1/bbl of widening in the WCS to WTI differential is worth $140 million a year to the company. The Lake Charles reserve exchange was not mentioned on the call, and its cause remains undisclosed. Freight's freshest prints corroborate the pressure while suggesting a peak: the US Gulf to Asia VLCC voyage was about $58 million on Oct 27 (McQuilling via RBN, Oct 29), level with the Baltic Oct 23 assessment after a record above $80 million in early October, and Vortexa (Oct 28) reads Atlantic discounts at record levels with Asia trades still uneconomic on freight. Cenovus announced Oct 28 that its third quarter results land Wednesday Nov 4 (call 8:30 a.m. ET), superseding the Oct 30 date this digest had carried; Imperial Oil is confirmed for Friday Oct 30.
changes.balance: The widest Canadian differentials of the episode are being priced by freight and returning competing supply, on the largest buyer's own testimony, while that buyer's system runs at record throughput on Canadian barrels. The constraint is delivered cost, not refinery appetite.
changes.conditional: Imperial's Friday volumes grade the synthetic return story, and Cenovus on Nov 4 grades the SAGD fleet. A Week 44 Baltic print showing the dirty correction extending would ease the freight leg of the differential; a re-acceleration would say the peak call was early.
changes.source: Phillips 66 release and earnings call, Oct 28, 2026; RBN Energy, Oct 29, 2026; Vortexa Freight Weekly, Oct 28, 2026; Cenovus announcement via GlobeNewswire, Oct 28, 2026; Imperial Oil announcement via Business Wire, Oct 20, 2026

changes.title: The waiver programme became a legal fight with three ships at sea, and DOE posted nothing again
changes.delta: The first waiver tanker has dropped New York as its declared destination and shows for orders off Denmark; three tankers hold 924,000 barrels combined, due at the US Atlantic coast Nov 7 to 11; a senator's letter sets an Oct 31 deadline for the first ship's owner to recall it and disclose the trade. DOE: no NEHHOR award, no award for either reserve exchange round, no new posted contracts total; SPR 282.6 Mbbl, a 44 year low.
changes.body: The tanker that loaded 40,000 tonnes of diesel at Primorsk on Oct 22 has dropped New York as its declared destination and shows for orders, reported idling off Skagen on Oct 26 (Lloyd's List via OilPrice, Oct 28); tracking services still project a New York arrival around Nov 7. Three tankers in total are at sea with 924,000 barrels of Russian diesel combined (Kpler via Splash247 and the Financial Times, Oct 28), expected Nov 7 to 11; two of the three are sanctioned by at least one of the US, EU or UK on the common core of the reporting, and the import licence does not cover sanctioned vessels (Gibson, Oct 26). A fourth tanker was expected to sail Oct 28 on a Russian deputy prime minister's statement; no verified sailing or name has been found. A US senator's Oct 27 letter demands the first ship's owner recall the vessel and disclose the seller, buyer, charterer, insurer and terminal operator by Oct 31, arguing the 2022 import ban bars the cargo regardless of the Treasury licence; seven lawmakers had written Oct 24 to six banks and four port authorities warning that handling the imports could bring legal action. DOE checked directly: nothing new posted Oct 28 to 29, no award for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange whose bids closed Oct 27 (deliveries due by Nov 13), no award published for the Sep 29 round or the Oct 16 re-offer of up to 17 Mbbl, and no new posted contracts total; the last verified tally stands at 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies. The reserve itself is 282.6 Mbbl, the lowest since October 1982 (EIA, Oct 28).
changes.balance: The November diesel tranche now has to clear lawyers before it clears a berth: the programme's announced supply (500,000 tonnes in November) is at sea or loading into an active legal challenge aimed at the banks and ports that would receive it, while the domestic reserve buffer sits at a 44 year low with its own exchange awards unpublished.
changes.conditional: The first tanker's declared destination changing back to a US port, or a discharge, settles whether the cargo lands; the Oct 31 response deadline shows whether the owner engages or defies. A DOE award posting for any of the three open rounds changes the reserve arithmetic directly.
changes.source: OilPrice, Oct 28, 2026; Splash247 and Financial Times, Oct 28, 2026; Gibson Shipbrokers, Oct 26, 2026; DOE pages checked directly, Oct 29, 2026; EIA, Oct 28, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz and Saudi claims: the Ras Tanura refinery claim is unconfirmed on day two; the strait authority threatens the largest carrier from Nov 1
flags.body: The Houthis claimed on Tuesday a missile hit on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery (550 kb/d); Saudi authorities have not confirmed it, a single unnamed source said a fire near the export terminal was contained with the damage extent unclear, and no reporting establishes a suspension of loadings, a berth closure or a quantified export loss. Early Thursday the coalition intercepted a new missile toward the Eastern Province, which is not a confirmation of the refinery claim. The flow gauges disagree on level and agree on direction: Vortexa's preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz run about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 pre-war, with about 6 Mb/d moving by ship to ship transfer, while Petro-Logistics counts strait transits plus bypass pipelines at about 18.8 Mb/d against 19.9 pre-war; the scopes differ and are not averaged. CENTCOM (Oct 28) says Iranian mine claims are false and the primary routes remain cleared. The dated risk is legal: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority says it will take legal action against all Sinokor vessels from Nov 1; Sinokor carried nearly 40 percent of September's Hormuz crude. Trade the loadings and the flow prints, not the claim count.
flags.trigger: A Saudi or Aramco statement of facility damage, loading evidence of a Ras Tanura flow interruption, enforcement action against a Sinokor vessel on or after Nov 1, or a tier 1 flow print stepping down

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: three cargoes at sea into a legal challenge; the first ship is not declaring a US destination
flags.body: Three tankers carrying 924,000 barrels of Russian diesel combined are at sea for the US Atlantic coast (arrivals projected Nov 7 to 11), and the first has dropped New York as its declared destination and shows for orders off Denmark. Two of the three vessels are sanctioned by at least one major list, which the import licence does not cover. Lawmakers have warned six banks and four port authorities that handling the imports could bring legal action, and a senator's letter sets an Oct 31 deadline for the first ship's owner to recall the vessel and disclose the trade's parties. A fourth sailing expected Oct 28 is unverified. The announced programme runs 500,000 tonnes in November; that tranche is the supply test, and it now has to clear the legal challenge before it clears a berth.
flags.trigger: A discharge at a US port, a declared destination change on any of the three vessels, the owner's Oct 31 response, a verified fourth sailing, or a Treasury or court ruling on the licence's reach

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights and 7 percent heavies; the December call is unregistered; December WCS at -$31.00 rests on 2 lots
flags.body: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20), with Light 13 percent at Cromer and Heavy 16 percent at Superior. December's nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7; no December judgment call is registered yet, and nominations close Nov 17. The front of the Canadian curve is pricing the constraint before the barrels arrive: December WCS settled at -$31.00 (ICE TMW, Oct 27) on only 2 lots, with January traded at -$29.30 on 235 lots and the delivered Gulf Coast differential at its weakest since October 2022 in last week's recap. The largest US buyer of Canadian crude testified on Oct 28 that heavy pricing is a race to the bottom driven mostly by freight, and that each $1 of WCS widening is worth $140 million a year to it. The level of the December print needs volume to be believed; the direction has traded corroboration.
flags.trigger: A December WCS settlement on real volume confirming or rejecting the -$31.00 level, Imperial and Cenovus third quarter volumes (Oct 30 and Nov 4), or the December apportionment notice after nominations close Nov 17

flags.title: Freight: the dirty correction is levelling near $58 million a voyage; clean tankers were at records in Week 43
flags.body: Week 43 (week ending Oct 23) remains the latest Baltic weekly: TD3C WS 1208.13 (TCE $1,287,851 per day), TD22 at $58.22 million, TD28 Vancouver to China at $14.26 million, and clean routes at records. The freshest evidence, McQuilling via RBN (Oct 29), has the US Gulf to Asia VLCC voyage at about $58 million on Oct 27, level with the Baltic assessment, down from a record above $80 million in early October; Aframax US Gulf to Europe has fallen from about WS 1,000 to about WS 720. Vortexa (Oct 28) assesses that freight has peaked in the short term but will not return to pre-war levels while transfer volumes and war risk premia persist, and that Atlantic discounts at record levels still do not make Asia trades economic. Whether the correction extends is a Week 44 question.
flags.trigger: The Baltic Week 44 weekly, a Gibson weekly confirming or rejecting the peak call, or a re-acceleration in TD3C or TD22

calendar.title: Imperial Oil Q3 results; CFTC commitments of traders release
calendar.impact: Imperial is the first Canadian volume check on the synthetic return verdict (call 9:00 a.m. MT). The positioning release updates the Oct 20 vintage.

calendar.title: Waiver cargo disclosure deadline
calendar.impact: The deadline in the Oct 27 senator's letter for the first waiver tanker's owner to recall the vessel and disclose the seller, buyer, charterer, insurer and terminal operator.

calendar.title: OPEC+ meeting; strait authority action date against Sinokor vessels
calendar.impact: OPEC+ is expected to hold December targets steady; only a deviation changes barrels. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority's threatened legal action against all Sinokor vessels starts this date; Sinokor carried nearly 40 percent of September's Hormuz crude.

calendar.title: Suncor Q3 results; US midterm elections
calendar.impact: Suncor operates Syncrude and the Base Plant and Edmonton refinery windows that ended in mid-October; its Q3 volumes are the closest public read on those returns ahead of September AER data. The midterms are the date after which US strike expectations on Iran have been priced.

calendar.title: Cenovus Q3 results (corrected date); Vermilion Q3 results
calendar.impact: Cenovus announced Oct 28 that it reports Nov 4 (call 8:30 a.m. ET), superseding the Oct 30 date previously carried. Christina Lake and the SAGD fleet's autumn volumes are the read. Vermilion reports the same day.

calendar.title: MEG Energy Q3 results
calendar.impact: MEG reports the September quarter; Christina Lake volumes are the read on the SAGD fleet's autumn.

calendar.title: Enbridge Q3 results
calendar.impact: Enbridge reports into the November apportionment month (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert); Mainline volumes and any December colour are the read.

calendar.title: First waiver cargo's projected US arrival window opens
calendar.impact: The three waiver tankers are projected at the US Atlantic coast between Nov 7 and Nov 11; the first ship currently declares no destination. A discharge would be the programme's first delivered barrel.

calendar.title: NEHHOR exchange deliveries complete
calendar.impact: Deliveries under the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids closed Oct 27, no award posted at this edition) complete by Nov 13, refilling the reserve ahead of the 2027 to 2028 heating season.

calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close (NOS day)
calendar.impact: Nominations for December close at 0700 MST. December's nowcast is persistence at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent; a judgment call registered before this date is the prediction programme's second decision performance entry.
